To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most consistent and reproducible supra-additive effects of c-DDP and X ray on the SCCVIII tumor are achieved by daily 2.4-mg/kg doses of c-DDP given 24 hr before daily 4-Gy fractions of X ray, and the most consistent supra-additive effects for mouse duodenum crypt cells and lung are achieved by daily c-DDP doses of 2 mg/kg given immediately before daily 4 Gy of X ray.
the supra-additive effects of c-DDP and X rays on the SCCVll tumor were greater than those on normal tissues and that the supra-additivity was dependent on the interval between drug and irradiation.

the combination of cisplatinum and radiation therapy produces supra-additive effects in the SCCVIII tumor of the C3HeB/FeJ mouse and that this effect is dependent on the interval between cisplatinum and irradiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a more effective treatment regimen using cis-diamminodichloroplatin II (c-DDPl) and radiation for the SCCVIII tumor.
the effects of fractionated radiation therapy and the interaction between radiation and chemotherapeutic agents in the treatment of cancer.
the development of new treatment schedules which can produce supra-additive therapeutic effects on the SCC VII tumor and normal tissues.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most promising combination treatment schedule is the single drug dose 1 day before the 5 daily X rays, and this schedule is also the least toxic.
c-DDP and radiation are synergistic for tumor cells and that the therapeutic gain is high.
c-DDP is a potentially useful drug for enhancing radiation effects, but that further studies are necessary to define the optimum schedule for clinical use
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most consistent and clinically relevant enhancement of the radiation effect on SCCVII tumor was produced by c-DDP when given before the first of the daily X ray fractions.
c-DDP is an effective radiosensitizer for tumors and normal tissues, but the therapeutic gain factor is high for tumors and low for normal tissues, which is a favorable result.
the most useful schedules are those with a 24-hr interval between X ray fractions and c-DDP administration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interval between drug and irradiation treatments is a critical determinant of the therapeutic gain factor (TGF) of a combined modality regimen.
the timing of c-DDP administration is important for the therapeutic gain factor.
the therapeutic gain factor (TGF) is a function of the tumor enhancement ratio (TER), the normal tissue enhancement ratio (NTER) and the ratio of the TER to the NTER (TGF = TER/NTER).
